content: Photocoagulation and anti-VEGF therapy have been shown to be effective in the management of diabetic macular edema. Specifically, anti-VEGF injections have demonstrated efficacy in improving visual acuity and reducing the necessity for laser treatments. Panretinal photocoagulation remains a proven method for preventing severe vision loss in patients with high-risk proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR). However, anti-VEGF therapy may provide additional advantages for patients who prefer or require a less invasive treatment approach.
